item.title: Sergey Brin says Google's AI models are reaching a critical moment of self-improvement
item.description:
Source: Business Insider
Google's co-founder Sergey Brin has stated that the company's AI models are nearing a critical phase of self-improvement, marking a pivotal moment in artificial intelligence development. During a roundtable discussion about the Gemini 4 model, Brin emphasized that AI systems are now accelerating their own evolution through recursive self-improvement (RSI), where models assist in building more advanced versions of themselves. This creates a 'flywheel' effect, speeding up the development of new models. Brin cited Google's earlier Flash models as evidence of this trend, noting the company is 'starting to get onto that RSI treadmill.' He highlighted collaboration between researchers and models to create the next iteration, with teams already ahead of public releases. A new report from Gladstone AI suggests most researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepMind believe RSI could begin within 3-12 months, potentially sooner without government intervention. Google's safety report for its Argon model noted AI agents are automating parts of the R&D cycle, authoring most production code and bug fixes, though human review remains required. Brin, who has prioritized RSI efforts at Google, expressed excitement about the rapid pace of development, with internal models like Carbon—tested by employees—compared to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 in coding tasks. Vihan Jain, an RSI leader at DeepMind, tweeted that the RSI flywheel has 'reached a new gear,' as demand for Argon resources shifted from hardware to model quotas. The article underscores growing industry consensus that AI systems are approaching a transformative phase of autonomous advancement.

item.title: Delta scores a small win in the airline WiFi wars
item.description:
Source: Business Insider
Delta Air Lines is improving its free WiFi service for transpacific routes, marking a small victory in the airline's ongoing competition for superior in-flight internet. The upgrade, part of Delta Sync, is set to launch this month, offering faster speeds compared to United Airlines' current offerings. Delta uses Viasat's VS-3 satellites, which provide over 1 terabit per second of capacity, including coverage for its transpacific flights via the F3 satellite launched in April. In contrast, United has been rapidly deploying Starlink technology, with over 40% of its fleet now equipped as of late 2024. United, which signed up for Starlink in 2024, aims to have all planes equipped by the end of next year, though only six of its 244 wide-body aircraft currently support the service. Long-haul flights to Asia remain limited, as Boeing 787-9s await FAA certification for Starlink. Elon Musk criticized Delta's decision to partner with Amazon's Leo satellite service instead of Starlink, urging CEO Ed Bastian to resign. United also lobbied customers by offering loyalty program perks to switch, claiming its WiFi is the fastest. While Delta's upgrade has received praise from travelers like Ben Bearup, who noted faster speeds on transpacific flights, United's aggressive Starlink rollout suggests it will maintain an edge until Amazon Leo becomes operational in 2028. Both airlines continue to compete in a race to deliver reliable, high-speed connectivity amid growing passenger demand.

item.title: I clean for my 92-year-old neighbor every week. I make $35 an hour — and we've become unlikely friends.
item.description:
Source: Business Insider
The article describes the author's experience as a weekly cleaner for her 92-year-old neighbor, highlighting the unique relationship that developed. The author, who works multiple side gigs, began cleaning the neighbor's home after a friend's mother connected her with the opportunity. The job involves cleaning twice a week for $35 an hour, with tasks including surface cleaning, floor maintenance, and larger projects like fridge organization. The author enjoys the routine, the solitude, and the sense of accomplishment from making a positive impact. She notes the importance of understanding the neighbor's preferences and learning about her lifestyle, such as the significance of the coffee machine in her daily routine. The arrangement has fostered an intergenerational friendship, with the author appreciating the neighbor's vintage decor and life insights. She reflects on the value of age-gap friendships, emphasizing mutual respect and shared time, such as watching Jeopardy! and discussing life. The author also mentions the physical benefits of the job, as it helps her stay active despite her sedentary main job as a therapist. The experience has reshaped her view of cleaning as more than a task, highlighting its role in building meaningful connections and preserving a home's history.
